title: Complexity of shape: slope entropy (a newly-authored op) completes the discrete-symbolic trio, bit-for-bit vs NeuroKit2

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The discrete-symbolic complexity folds so far symbolize amplitude patterns (dispersion) or increment magnitudes (increment entropy). Slope entropy (Cuesta-Frau 2019) symbolizes the SLOPE ANGLE between successive samples into five classes (steep/gentle/flat, up/down) and takes the entropy of the slope patterns -- capturing the shape of local trends. The ecosystem lacked it; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, slopeEntropy, completing the discrete-symbolic trio (NCDF-dispersion / increment-magnitude / slope-angle). On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel it reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_slope BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~9e-16) across the embedding dimension; unlike the normalized entropies it INCREASES with dimension (1.26 -> 2.43 -> 3.57, unnormalized Shannon over longer patterns), and the signal realizes 18 of the 25 = 5^(m-1) possible slope patterns at m=3.

claims.statement: slope entropy at m=2 (thresholds 0.1/45 deg) of the POz signal (bits)
slope entropy at m=3 -- higher than m=2 (increasing in dimension)
slope entropy at m=4 -- higher still (unnormalized, grows with pattern length)
max |slopeEntropy - NeuroKit2 entropy_slope| over the embedding dimension (bit-exact)
distinct slope patterns realized at m=3 (out of 5^(m-1) = 25 possible)
SlopEn INCREASES with the embedding dimension (1 = holds; contrast with normalized entropies)

validation.reference: The newly-authored slopeEntropy op is validated against NeuroKit2 entropy_slope across the embedding dimension. NeuroKit2 re-computes the slope entropy from the identical slope-angle thresholding + pattern-count + Shannon pipeline; the agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~9e-16). On real eyes-closed POz EEG SlopEn increases with dimension (1.26 -> 2.43 -> 3.57) and the signal realizes 18 of the 25 (=5^(m-1)) possible slope patterns at m=3.
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored slopeEntropy reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_slope bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~9e-16) across the embedding dimension; (2) it increases with dimension (unnormalized) and the signal realizes 18 of 25 possible slope patterns at m=3. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a gap -- the ecosystem had amplitude, NCDF-pattern, template-matching and increment-magnitude entropies but not the slope-angle symbolic entropy; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op and NeuroKit2 compute the IDENTICAL slope-angle thresholding + pattern-count + Shannon pipeline, so the ~9e-16 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) the mechanism is genuinely distinct: SlopEn combines a coarse (steep/gentle) and fine (flat) angular resolution to capture the SHAPE of local trends, completing the discrete-symbolic complexity trio (NCDF-dispersion / increment-magnitude / slope-angle); (4) unlike the normalized entropies (increment/fuzzy, which decrease with m), SlopEn is an UNNORMALIZED Shannon over length-(m-1) patterns, so it INCREASES with the embedding dimension -- an informative structural contrast; (5) the value depends on (dimension, thresholds); here the NeuroKit2 defaults (m=3, thresholds 0.1/45 deg), so the reproducible content is the bit-exact family and the pattern structure, not an absolute physiological constant; (6) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: Slope entropy's angular thresholds are its knobs: the flat threshold (0.1 deg) separates true plateaus from micro-drift, and the steep threshold (45 deg) the fast transitions. Sweeping the thresholds (a 'slope-entropy profile') and comparing across EEG states or channels would turn the single value into a shape-sensitive fingerprint; Cuesta-Frau (2019) shows the thresholds can be tuned for class separability. Documented, not escalated.
